purpose: SEC-DB-RLS-001 I1: the target database identity model. Explicit grants, no default privileges: a table that is not listed here gets no runtime access (fails closed) and the verifier fails CI until it is classified. Nothing in this file is applied to production by I1.

identities.vexa_migrator: owns every object in the public schema and runs migrations (deploy time only); NOSUPERUSER, BYPASSRLS because tables are FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and data-fixing migrations must see every tenant; an owner can disable RLS regardless, so this adds no isolation risk; never held by the runtime path
identities.vexa_runtime: the API; table-level privileges from runtime.tables; owns nothing; no DDL; NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS
identities.vexa_backup: read-only; BYPASSRLS is its only extra attribute, justified solely because pg_dump must read forced-RLS tables; SELECT only
identities.vexa_reporter: read-only operator reports that span tenants (the sellable-SKU audit report and the media-integrity report); NOSUPERUSER; BYPASSRLS only because a report spans tenants; SELECT on the report tables only; owns nothing, no DDL, no writes; its credential must never be reachable by the API process
identities.vexa_ops: operator path: the platform control tables (the kill switch and the platform budget periods) and the sellable-SKU backfill; NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS, so the backfill sets the tenant context itself and iterates tenants; it is never a general cross-tenant writer

noCrossTenantMaintenanceRole: Deliberately not provisioned, and no policy may open on a session setting that the ordinary runtime can set. Cross-tenant jobs that run inside the API use tenant iteration (docs/qa/sec-db-rls-001-call-site-classification-2026-10-06.md section 3, owner decision 2026-10-07 on D-022). A cross-tenant read that cannot iterate runs outside the API as an operator script under the read-only vexa_reporter; a cross-tenant write iterates tenants under vexa_ops. No BYPASSRLS maintenance role is created to preserve a shortcut.

exceptionsToCrud.ai_platform_controls: SELECT only: operators write the kill switch through vexa_ops, never the API
exceptionsToCrud.ai_platform_budget_periods: SELECT and UPDATE only: the API moves counters, operators create and delete periods
exceptionsToCrud.connector_definitions: SELECT only (SEC-DB-RLS-001 8.1a): the catalogue of connectors is reference data written by migrations and operator seeds; no API code path writes it (searched: typed accessors, raw SQL, nested writes), and the restricted-role lane runs the API without write access
exceptionsToCrud.connector_tenant_entitlements: SELECT only (SEC-DB-RLS-001 8.1a): an append-only grant ledger (a trigger forbids edits) written by Product Operations, never by the API; the publication-target evaluator only reads it
exceptionsToCrud.tax_regimes: SELECT only (SEC-DB-RLS-001 8.1b): a system registry of tax regimes (no RLS) read by catalog and bulk-import validation; the only writers are the deploy-time seed (scripts/seed-tax-regimes.cjs, which writes as vexa_migrator once MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL is set) and test-environment seeds
exceptionsToCrud.audit_logs: SELECT and INSERT only (SEC-DB-RLS-001 8.2): the audit trail: the API appends and reads; no code path edits or deletes it (typed accessors, raw SQL and nested writes searched). Only an administrator seed script deletes rows, in test environments
exceptionsToCrud.account_consent_events: SELECT and INSERT only (SEC-DB-RLS-001 8.2): the consent ledger: events are appended and read; no code path edits or deletes one, and the account-deletion worker touches only MFA enrolments, identities and the deletion request
exceptionsToCrud.kpi_metric_events: SELECT and INSERT only (SEC-DB-RLS-001 8.2): metric events are appended and aggregated by reading; nothing updates or deletes them
exceptionsToCrud.approval_comments: SELECT and INSERT only (SEC-DB-RLS-001 8.2): approval comments are appended and listed; there is no edit or delete path, and the table has no foreign keys, so a product deletion neither cascades into it nor needs to
exceptionsToCrud.connector_mapping_events: SELECT and INSERT only (SEC-DB-RLS-001 8.2): the mapping history ledger: events are appended (create and createMany) and read; nothing edits or deletes one. Its only foreign key (to connector_mapping_versions, ON DELETE CASCADE) cascades under the table owner, which the rehearsal proves needs no DELETE privilege for the runtime; no application code deletes mapping versions

ops.note: Product and Variant serve the sellable-SKU backfill (scripts/sellable-sku-variantless-backfill.cjs reads products, reads and creates variants). Both are forced-RLS tables and vexa_ops is NOBYPASSRLS, so the backfill must set the tenant context for each tenant. WorkspaceDirectory (SELECT only, no RLS) is where it lists those tenants; without it a restricted role would have to guess the tenant list, or see only the default tenant.

reporter.note: The audit report reads connectorSubmission, product and variant (scripts/sellable-sku-variantless-audit-report.cjs); the media-integrity report reads mediaAsset (scripts/media-integrity-readonly-report.cjs). Read-only, across tenants by design.

public.note: SEC-DB-RLS-001 8.3. PUBLIC holds nothing beyond the table rules above: no CONNECT, TEMPORARY or CREATE on the database, no USAGE or CREATE on schema public, no EXECUTE on any function and no USAGE on any enum type. Every identity connects and uses the schema through an EXPLICIT grant; nobody creates temporary tables. Two facts about PostgreSQL decide what is NOT granted, and the rehearsal proves both: a trigger function needs no EXECUTE for the trigger to fire (only creating the trigger checks it), and USAGE on a type does not control using its values in queries or casts (it only controls creating objects that depend on the type), so the application, which creates no such objects, needs no USAGE on the enum types. The migrator owns them.
public.database: no PUBLIC privilege; every identity has CONNECT and none has TEMPORARY
public.schema: no PUBLIC privilege; every identity has USAGE; only the migrator has CREATE
public.types: no USAGE for PUBLIC and none for any identity but the owner (the migrator): the application only queries enum values
